clue.text: Ultimately joyless sex in retirement, tender embraces from behind prove unsettling

indicators.note: embraces means holds within its arms, so one piece wraps round the others
the word for tender is read from its back end, so it is written backwards

parts.note: to tender is to bid, as at an auction or for a contract

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of joyless
retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word for sex is written backwards

parts.note: rut is the season of sexual activity in deer, so sex here

explanation.surface: A jaded lover's complaint: sex has gone dull with age, and even tender hugs from behind feel unsettling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex' reads as the act; here it is the rut, the deer's mating season. 'from behind' and 'in retirement' both signal reversals, and 'embraces' the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb or upset someone is to prove unsettling to them, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Skilful wrapping each in foil

indicators.note: wrapping means going round, so the word for skilful encloses the abbreviation

parts.note: deft means skilful, nimble with the hands
ea is the usual abbreviation for each, as on price lists

explanation.surface: A deft cook wraps each portion in kitchen foil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foil' looks like kitchen foil continuing the wrapping picture, but it is the verb meaning thwart.
explanation.definitionFit: To foil a plan is to thwart or beat it, so the verb is a synonym.

clue.text: Hot and moist, place cakes wearily at first on base of tray

indicators.note: cakes as a verb means coats or encases, so the word for place surrounds a letter

parts.note: a seat is a place, as in taking your place at a table

indicators.note: at first selects the opening letter of wearily
the base of a down-clue word is its last letter, here of tray

explanation.surface: A tired baker wearily sets out cakes on a tray in a hot, humid kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cakes' looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning encrusts, putting W inside SEAT; 'on' puts Y at the bottom of this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone perspiring is hot and damp with perspiration, a dictionary match.

clue.text: Hidden uranium has affected nerve cord

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters of nerve cord are rearranged

explanation.surface: A medical report: exposure to uranium has damaged a patient's nerve cord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' signals the rearrangement; 'has' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Undercover work is secret or concealed, so the word means hidden.

clue.text: A hundred bunk beds for artist

indicators.note: beds means puts to bed or embeds, so the nonsense word takes the numeral inside

parts.note: bunk is nonsense, as is bosh
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A hundred bunk beds seem a strange subject for a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bunk beds' reads as furniture, but bunk is nonsense and 'beds' is the verb meaning embeds. Bosch is the Dutch painter Hieronymus Bosch.
explanation.definitionFit: Hieronymus Bosch was a Netherlandish painter famous for fantastical scenes, so an example of an artist.

clue.text: See 14
Creative thinker in rock star's overcome

indicators.note: is overcome means has something above it, so in this down entry the star sits over the rock

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares in brightness
a tor is a rocky hill or outcrop, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A creative thinker who happens to be in a rock star's entourage has been overwhelmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock star' reads as a musician, but the two words split; ''s overcome' places the star above the rock in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovator introduces new ideas or methods, making them a creative thinker.

clue.text: See 26
Asian in time standing for self-centredness

indicators.note: in signals the Asian person going inside the reversed word
standing means upright, so in a down entry the word for time reads upwards

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
an Omani is someone from Oman, a country in Asia

explanation.surface: An Asian person stood in for someone at the time, a selfless act rather than self-centred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' means upright, so in a down entry the word for time reads upwards; 'in' then signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive preoccupation with oneself is egomania, a near synonym of self-centredness.

clue.text: Link again on chains even, funny

indicators.note: chains means binds or holds fast, so the word for on encloses the rest

parts.note: re means on, about or concerning
e'en is the poetic contraction of even
a funny is a joke, and so is a gag

explanation.surface: A jeweller links a chain again, though the even result looks a bit funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' wants to be an anagram signal; here it is a noun, a joke. 'chains' is the enclosing signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage again is to take up or connect once more, so a synonym for linking again.

clue.text: See 14
Country music performer pitiful to hear?

indicators.note: to hear means as it sounds when spoken, so these words are said aloud

parts.note: a singer is a musical performer; poor means pitiful or wretched

explanation.surface: A country music performer whose playing is pitiful to listen to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country music' looks like the genre; 'Country' is the definition, and the music performer stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore is an island city-state in Southeast Asia, an example of a country.

clue.text: Sweet to eat something fragrant

parts.note: afters is British slang for the sweet course, dessert
to have a meal is to eat it

explanation.surface: A dessert offered to eat that smells lovely.
explanation.walkthrough: AFTERS is British informal for the pudding course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-shave lotion is a scented product, so it is something fragrant.

clue.text: Fringe cut straight, precisely

definitions.meaning: in American usage, a fringe of hair cut straight across the forehead
exactly, as in arriving ... on time

explanation.surface: A hairdresser cuts a fringe dead straight, with precision.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a straight-cut fringe, and the informal adverb means exactly, as in bang on.

clue.text: Novelty act had tune for single

indicators.note: novelty means something new, so the letters of act had tune are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A novelty act had a tune released as a single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' looks like a record release continuing the pop picture, but it means unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not in a relationship is single, an everyday synonym.

clue.text: Where scarecrows are doing a great job?

definitions.text: Where scarecrows are doing a great job?

parts.words: Where scarecrows are doing a great job?
parts.note: scarecrows literally stand outdoors among the crops, and the idiom for excelling at one's work describes them literally

explanation.surface: A question about where scarecrows are most effective.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means excellent at one's profession; read literally it describes a scarecrow standing out in a farmer's crop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom praises an expert as excelling in their profession, which is doing a great job.

clue.text: Routine quavering made in warble

indicators.note: in signals the shaken letters sitting inside the word for warble

parts.note: a trill is a warble, a quavering run of notes

indicators.note: quavering means trembling or wavering, so the letters of made are shaken up

explanation.surface: A singer's quavering voice in the middle of a warble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quavering' signals the anagram and 'in' the insertion; 'Routine' looks like a musical routine but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadmill is a dull, unvarying routine, from the figurative sense of endless walking going nowhere.

clue.text: Last of rabbits with hare, say, in a stew

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of rabbits

parts.note: hare sounds like hair, and having hair is tressed

explanation.surface: A recipe: rabbit and hare stewed together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks hare as a sound-alike for hair; tressed means having tresses, with hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In a stew is an idiom for anxious or worked up, which is what stressed means.

clue.text: Wood and silicate not entirely vinegary?

parts.note: balsa is a very light wood used in models

indicators.note: not entirely means one letter short, so the end of the silicate's name is dropped

parts.note: mica is a silicate mineral that splits into thin sheets

explanation.surface: Wood and silicate don't seem to taste of vinegar at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' drops the final A from MICA. The question mark flags that the definition is an example rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsamic vinegar is a dark Italian vinegar, so the adjective describes something like vinegar, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Setter cared to mess around? That's none of your business!

indicators.note: messing around means jumbling things up, so the letters of setter cared are rearranged

explanation.surface: The puzzle setter cared to fool about, and when asked why, snapped back that it was private.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter here is the compiler of the puzzle, Paul himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A confidential method a firm keeps to itself is not for outsiders to know, so it is none of your business.

clue.text: Prepared to embrace poet, no alternative

indicators.note: alternative means offering another version, so the letters of poet no are given in another order

explanation.surface: A publisher is ready to take on a poet, having no other option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no alternative' reads as a phrase meaning no choice, but 'no' is fodder and 'alternative' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being receptive to an idea means being willing to accept or welcome it.

clue.text: Key once more accessing sleepy terrace from the basement?

indicators.note: from the basement means read from the bottom upwards in this down entry
accessing means getting inside, so the letters come from within sleepy terrace

explanation.surface: Someone gets into a sleepy terrace via the basement with a duplicate key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accessing' takes EPYTER from inside sleepy terrace; 'from the basement' reads it upwards. 'Key' is the verb meaning type on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To key is to type on a keyboard, so keying again is typing it a second time.

clue.text: See 25
Lump in throat, as computer giant in the hands of sinner?

indicators.note: in the hands of means belonging to, so the owner's name comes first, possessive

parts.note: Adam was the first sinner in Genesis, and 'in the hands of' makes him the owner, Adam's
Apple is a huge computer company

explanation.surface: Emotion catches in the throat when a computer giant falls into a sinner's hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lump in throat' looks like the emotional choke; it is the literal laryngeal bulge. Eating the apple was Adam's sin.
explanation.definitionFit: The visible bulge of the larynx in the neck is a lump in the throat, especially in men.

clue.text: Big cheese mound

definitions.meaning: an important, powerful person, a tycoon
a bump of hard snow on a ski slope

explanation.surface: A big cheese and a mound, as of a large wheel on a platter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a powerful magnate and a hump of snow on a ski run.

clue.text: Basic unit 1-13 of 26?

parts.note: the first of the alphabet's twenty-six letters is A
a dash between two numbers is read as to, as in pages 1-13
the thirteenth of the alphabet's twenty-six letters is M

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that looks like it points at clue numbers in the grid.
explanation.walkthrough: '26' looks like a reference to 26 across, but it is the alphabet's 26 letters, and 1-13 are A to M.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest basic unit of a chemical element.

clue.text: Not that great

definitions.meaning: informal praise for ... remarkable or exceptional

explanation.surface: A grudging verdict: not that great.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a different thing, and colloquially also an outstanding thing.

clue.text: Alluring lure, perfect individual served up

parts.note: to hone a skill is to perfect it

indicators.note: served up means presented upwards, so the word for individual is read backwards

parts.note: a party is an individual person, as in legal documents or the guilty party

explanation.surface: A tempting lure: the perfect person served up on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect individual' reads as an ideal person, but 'perfect' is a verb; 'served up' turns PARTY into YTRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A seductive scheme to entrap a target with romance is an alluring kind of lure.

clue.text: There's a point to this medical treatment

indicators.note: treatment means handling or processing, so the letters of medical are worked over

explanation.surface: Someone insists the medical treatment does have a purpose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'point' looks like purpose; it is the dot in a decimal number.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal number contains a decimal point, so there is literally a point to it.

clue.text: Back to steal a pilotless craft, old thief

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of steal

parts.note: a drone is an aircraft with no pilot on board

explanation.surface: A thief plans to steal back a pilotless aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Ladrone is an archaic word for a robber or brigand.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladrone is an archaic term for a robber or bandit, so an old word for thief.
